newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nordenham closure designed to stabilise output.
newsitem.headline: Nordenham closure designed to stabilise output.

text.p: A new shutdown of Metaleurop's lead furnace at Nordenham, Germany, will help stabilise production at the recently overhauled plant, the company said on Thursday.

Metaleurop, a French-based subsidiary of Germany's Preussag , said earlier it had halted production at the plant at the end of 1996. This was for repairs and adjustments expected to last until the final week of January.
"The production process which is not yet stabilised should be further improved by these measures," Metaleurop said in a statement.
The work involves partial repair of the refractory and other technical adjustments, it said.
The smelter started production in March last year but was closed between the end of July and the first week of September to allow extra modifications to be carried out.
Metaleurop had originally hoped to have the plant running at 70 percent of its 90,000 tonnes capacity during the first year of operation.
But following a series of recurring technical problems, the company said in September it was unlikely to reach this target.
Metaleurop gave no new production figures with Thursday's announcement.
It said lead deliveries to customers would not be affected because the refinery would process lead bullion from outside.
